The chapters follow LESSON["lecture"] in content/lesson-9.py part by part and in its words: the six rocks of the explore step (granite, chalk, sandstone, marble, slate, pumice, under the lesson's own tap cards); the coin, water and hand-lens tests of the tester step and the soak-up table of the record step; the quarry, the mine and the riverbed of the demo step (ART.scene extract 0-2); rock doing jobs on a roof, a wall, a path, a floor and a board, and the brick that people make; and the help-or-harm sort, with the old quarry that becomes a lake.
title: Rocks and the Earth
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Describe and compare different types of rock.
Know rocks are extracted from the Earth in different ways, including from quarries, mines and riverbeds.
Know that human activity can affect the environment.
Know that materials can be tested to determine their properties.

beats.say: Under the soil, the land is made of rock.
There are many kinds of rock. People dig it out and use it.
Granite is very hard. It has speckles of different colours.
Chalk is soft and white. It crumbles, and you can write with it.
Sandstone is grainy, like sand stuck together.
Marble is smooth and shiny when polished.
Slate is dark. It splits into thin flat sheets.
Pumice is full of holes. It is so light that it floats on water.
Not all rock is grey and hard. Not all rock is the same.

at.same: Not all rock is the same

beats.say: Test a rock to find its properties. A property is what it is like.
Scratch it with a coin. Chalk scratches, but granite is too hard.
Drop water on it. Does the water soak in, or run off?
Chalk and sandstone soak it up. Granite and marble do not.
Look with a hand lens. Is it grainy, smooth, or full of holes?
Every rock has its own properties. Testing finds them.
Rock is not made in a factory. It is dug out of the Earth.
A quarry is a huge open pit. Rock is cut and blasted out in blocks.
A mine is tunnels deep underground. Miners with lamps dig the rock out.
A riverbed is where water has worn rock into pebbles.
The smooth pebbles and gravel are scooped out.
Look around you. Rock is everywhere, doing jobs.
Slate on roofs. Stone in walls. Gravel on paths.
Marble on floors, and chalk on the board.
All of it began in a quarry, a mine or a river.
But a brick is not rock. People make bricks.
The environment is everything around us: land, water, air and living things.
Dumping rubbish in a river, smoke, concrete on a meadow: these harm.
Planting trees, recycling, keeping streams clean: these help.
A quarry is not only bad. An old one can become a lake for wildlife.
Ask: is the land, water or air better or worse after this?
Rocks are not all the same. Testing finds their properties.
Rock is taken from quarries, mines and riverbeds. We use it everywhere.
What we do changes the Earth. It can help the land, or harm it.
